interest: This document reflects interwar American vigilance and sensitivity regarding Japanese strategic intentions in Central America and the approaches to the Panama Canal. Despite consisting only of a list of papers sheet, it records diplomatic monitoring of rumors and anonymous tips alleging Japanese efforts to obtain a naval base in the strategically vital Gulf of Fonseca. It also serves as an important archival trail, directing historians to related military and intelligence files under decimal file 894.20216/7.
overview: This file consists of a single-page Department of State 'List of Papers' docket sheet for decimal file classification 894.34517 (also marked 894.24517), which encompasses Japanese naval equipment, supplies, and potential naval and coaling stations in Nicaragua. The solitary recorded entry documents Despatch No. 564 from January 22, 1936, sent by U.S. Minister Frank P. Corrigan in El Salvador. The despatch concerned an anonymous letter reporting on Japanese activities in Central America, specifically an alleged proposal to grant the Japanese government a naval base in the Gulf of Fonseca, with the original papers cross-referenced to file 894.20216/7.

subfiles.about: A State Department list of papers entry recording a diplomatic despatch concerning an anonymous report of Japanese naval base ambitions in the Gulf of Fonseca.
subfiles.summary: This single-page list of papers docket records Despatch No. 564 sent on January 22, 1936, by U.S. diplomat Frank P. Corrigan from El Salvador. The purport summarizes an anonymous letter concerning Japanese activities, notably an alleged scheme to grant the Imperial Japanese Government a naval facility in the Gulf of Fonseca. The record notes that the document itself was filed under decimal file 894.20216/7.
